t: The Catalan counties united under the counts of Barcelona, who were also kings of Aragon from 1162.
Its Corts, Generalitat and merchant capital Barcelona made it one of the most commercial and parliamentary states of medieval Europe.
Revolts in 1640 and 1705 ended in defeat, and the Nueva Planta decree of 1716 abolished its institutions.
dyk: The Taula de Canvi, founded by Barcelona’s city council in 1401, was one of the first public banks in Europe, holding deposits and handling the city’s finances.
ev: Alfonso II inherits Barcelona and Aragon, uniting them in the Crown of Aragon
Treaty of Corbeil: France renounces its claims over the Catalan counties
Peter III promises to summon the Catalan Corts every year
The Corts of Cervera create the Diputació del General, later the Generalitat
Civil war between the Generalitat and John II
The Reapers’ War breaks out with the Corpus de Sang in Barcelona
Barcelona falls to Philip V’s army on 11 September
The Nueva Planta decree abolishes Catalonia’s institutions
